title: Uptime brief and handoff matrix — 2029-04-05
content:
Purpose:
Quick weekly snapshot for SRE: incidents since last checkin, SLO health, and a compact handoff matrix for the upcoming rotation. This is intentionally terse for fast scanning during the Friday ops sync and weekend handoffs.

TL;DR:
- Overall 30d availability (prod) = 99.93% (below target 99.95%).
- Two P1-ish pages in 72 hours: cache-layer collision and autoscaler misconfiguration.
- Key follow-ups: KV cache eviction policy change (short-term), autoscaler max-burst guard (medium-term).
- Weekend on-call: Mateo (primary), Claire (secondary), escalation to Omar.

1) Incidents (chronological, short):
- 2029-04-03 03:21 UTC — INC-4872 — "cache key namespace collision"
  - Symptom: elevated 5xxs from hosted-api edge; correlated spikes in cache miss storm for a small subset of models.
  - Root cause (initial): a recent deploy introduced a namespace prefix regression in prefix-shard code path; two tenants' keys collided under high concurrency.
  - Mitigation: rolled back the deploy, increased prefix entropy, warmed cache for impacted models.
  - Impact: ~14 minutes of increased tail latency and 0.6% error rate spike on region us-west-2.
  - Action items: SRE-2123 (add unit/integration test for prefix collision). Assigned: Claire. ETA: 2029-04-12.

- 2029-04-04 18:40 UTC — "autoscaler burst overshoot"
  - Symptom: sudden CPU contention on dedicated pools, autoscaler launched more instances than quota allowed, causing transient throttles and request rejections.
  - Root cause: mis-read of provider API response when region returned partial fulfillment; logic treated partial as success.
  - Mitigation: applied hotfix to treat partial as partial, enabled fallback to reserved pool, and temporarily raised alert thresholds.
  - Impact: ~7 minutes of rejected requests for a small customer batch.
  - Action items: Create guard to prevent >N launches/sec (JIRA: SRE-2178). Assigned: Omar. ETA: 2029-04-19.

Minor items: ongoing tokenization pipeline lag (non-customer-impacting), observed during nightly batch window — note to investigate if it's correlated with embedding-index compaction. Owner: Priya.

2) SLO Health snapshot (past 30 days):
- Availability (prod global): 99.93% (SLO: 99.95%) — primary deficiency: two short bursts described above.
- P99 latency (text.generate): 420ms (target 350ms) — tail impacted during cache miss cascades.
- Error rate (user-facing 5xx): 0.25% (target 0.2%).
- Observations: most violations are small windowed spikes; trending upward during peak traffic hours.

3) Handoff matrix (compact) — upcoming weekend (2029-04-06 to 2029-04-08):
- Friday 17:00 PST -> Saturday 09:00 PST:
  - Primary: Mateo Ruiz (pager + phone)
  - Secondary: Claire Huang (pager)
  - Escalation: Omar Bennett (pager + call)
  - Notes: Mateo will shadow rollback plan for model-serving deploys; Claire to watch cache warmers.
- Saturday 09:00 PST -> Sunday 09:00 PST:
  - Primary: Claire Huang
  - Secondary: Priya Desai
  - Escalation: Anjali Patel (owner)
  - Notes: watch for autoscaler regression aftermath; verify new hotfix telemetry.
- Sunday 09:00 PST -> Monday 09:00 PST:
  - Primary: Priya Desai
  - Secondary: Mateo Ruiz
  - Escalation: Omar Bennett
  - Notes: runlight maintenance window planned for Sunday 02:00-03:00 UTC; non-disruptive expected.

4) Playbook changes / Quick wins (proposed tweaks):
- Short term (this sprint):
  - Add a sanity check in deploy pipeline that exercises cache prefix generation under concurrency (unit + integration). (Claire)
  - Add autoscaler partial-response handling test; introduce burst-rate limiter at controller. (Omar)
  - Raise SLO alert sensitivity for repeated small spikes — alert only after 3 consecutive 1-min windows (reduce noise). (Anjali)

- Medium term (next 1–2 sprints):
  - Implement adaptive KV-cache prewarming for high-QPS model variants. (Priya + infra)
  - Revisit autoscaler backoff heuristics with provider quotas in mind; simulation harness for partial allocations. (Platform-eng)

- Long term:
  - Consider soft-triage routing: on overload, route lower-priority requests to a cheaper quantized model to preserve SLOs for high-priority traffic. (Product + Serving Runtime)

5) Retrospective snippets (lessons learned):
- Regression origin is often a small change in shared util (prefix generation) — emphasize broader test harness that runs util code at scale during CI.
- Partial provider responses are a first-class failure mode; include in chaos test matrix.
- Observability: need a simpler way to correlate cache-hit-rate delta with downstream request tail latency — likely a dashboard tile and an alert.

6) Action item ledger (short):
- SRE-2123: Prefix collision test + CI gating — Claire Huang — ETA 2029-04-12.
- SRE-2178: Autoscaler burst guard + test harness — Omar Bennett — ETA 2029-04-19.
- SRE-2184: Cache prewarm experiment plan — Priya Desai — ETA 2029-04-26.
- DOC-119: Weekend handoff quick-reference (slim runbook) — Mateo Ruiz — ETA 2029-04-07.
- MON-54: Dashboard tile: cache-hit delta vs tail latency — Observability team — Owner: Anjali Patel — ETA 2029-04-18.

7) Meeting notes / decisions from this week's ops sync (2029-04-05 16:00 UTC):
- Agreed to throttle autoscaler launch rate for all regions as temporary guard. (decision)
- Agreed to run a targeted canary of the prefix fix against one low-traffic customer before full roll. (decision)
- Priya to run a 2-hour load test simulating model churn tomorrow to validate cache-warming heuristics. (decision + owner)

8) Known unknowns / flagged risks:
- If cache warmers can't keep up at 10k QPS churn, we may need a short-term admission control policy that rejects large-burst model loads.
- Provider-side partial fills may become more frequent as we add more regions — need contract with infra partners.

9) Notes to self (ops shorthand):
- When paging on cache collisions: immediately check prefix entropy histogram (query telemetry.index.assignments).
- For autoscale: check provider allocation event logs and compare to controller expectations (provider.alloc.trace).

10) Useful links / Slack threads:
- Slack: #sre-ops (thread: "cache collision 2029-04-03")
- Monitoring dashboard: https://monitoring.redwood/influx/dashboards/uptime-brief-2029-04
- Runbook (short): Confluence: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=74321

Appendix (raw quick metrics snapshot):
- 30d availability windows: 99.93%
- 7d availability windows: 99.82% (notably lower due to recent events)
- p99 latency (text.generate): 420ms
- 5xx rate (last 24h): 0.4% at peaks

If anything urgent pops during the weekend: call escalation list in order (Mateo -> Omar -> Anjali). If degraded SLO beyond 15 minutes, follow emergency protocol (see DOC-119).

End of brief.
